en.name: Orange juice, frozen concentrate
en.summary: A sealed tub of frozen orange juice concentrate keeps 12 months from purchase in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Once the can is opened and the concentrate is made up with water, it keeps up to 1 week in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: There is no room-temperature storage for frozen concentrate — it is a frozen product and belongs in the freezer from the shop to the kitchen. If a tub has thawed on the way home, do not refreeze it: make it up and refrigerate it, and use it within the window for prepared juice. Concentrate that has been left out and has separated or smells fermented should be discarded rather than salvaged.
en.fridge: The fridge is for the made-up juice rather than the concentrate. Once the can is opened and the concentrate is mixed with water it keeps up to 1 week at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, capped, on a shelf rather than in the door. The fridge is also the right place to soften a rock-hard tub slowly if you are making it up later in the day. Do not leave a tub of concentrate to thaw on the counter.
en.freezer: 12 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), in the sealed tub. Concentrate is a genuinely useful thing to keep: the water has been taken out, so a small tub replaces a large carton in the freezer, and the flavour holds up well because the juice was frozen close to pressing. Keep the tub at the back of the freezer rather than in the door, where the temperature swings every time it opens.
en.thawing: Soften the tub in the fridge, or run the sealed tub under cold water, then mix with cold water to the ratio on the label. Never thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze concentrate that has thawed.
spoilage: A fermented, yeasty or alcoholic smell from the tub or the made-up juice.
Fizzing when poured, which means fermentation has started.
Mould on the surface of made-up juice or around the neck of the jug.
A tub that is swollen or leaking, or one that has obviously thawed and refrozen.
tips: Keep the tub at the back of the freezer, not in the door.
Make it up with cold water and chill it before serving; it tastes better cold.
Make up only what you will drink within the week.
Freeze made-up juice in an ice-cube tray if you only want it for cooking or cocktails.

faq.q: How long does frozen orange juice concentrate keep?
faq.a: 12 months from purchase in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F) in its sealed tub.

faq.q: How long does made-up concentrate last?
faq.a: Once the can is opened and mixed with water, up to 1 week in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
No. Make it up, refrigerate it and drink it within the week for the prepared juice.

zh.name: 冷凍濃縮柳橙汁
zh.summary: 未開封的冷凍濃縮柳橙汁，自購買日起放 −18 °C 冷凍可放 12 個月。開封、加水沖調成可飲用的果汁之後，冷藏 4 °C 以下最多可放 1 週。
zh.pantry: 冷凍濃縮汁沒有常溫保存這一項——它是冷凍食品，從店裡到家裡都該待在冷凍狀態。如果回家路上已經退冰，就不要再冷凍：直接沖調好、放冷藏，並在沖調後果汁的期限內喝完。放在外面已經分離、或聞起來有發酵味的濃縮汁，請直接丟掉，不要想辦法救。
zh.fridge: 冰箱冷藏是給「沖調好的果汁」，不是給濃縮汁本身。開封、加水調好之後，蓋好放 4 °C 以下，最多 1 週，放層架而不是冰箱門。如果打算晚點才沖調，冷藏也是慢慢軟化整罐冰硬濃縮汁的正確位置。不要把整罐濃縮汁放在檯面上退冰。
zh.freezer: 原罐密封放 −18 °C，自購買日起 12 個月。濃縮汁其實很好用：水被抽掉了，一小罐就能取代冷凍庫裡一大盒的位置；而且因為果汁在榨取後很快就被冷凍，風味保持得相當好。請放冷凍庫深處，不要放門邊——那裡每開一次門溫度就晃一次。
zh.thawing: 請放冷藏慢慢軟化，或整罐密封著沖冷水，再依照標示比例加冷水調勻。絕對不要放檯面上退冰；退冰過的濃縮汁也不要再冷凍。
spoilage: 罐子或調好的果汁有發酵味、酵母味或酒味。
倒出來起泡，代表發酵已經開始。
調好的果汁液面或壺口長霉。
罐身鼓脹、滲漏，或明顯退冰後又被凍回去的痕跡。
tips: 罐子放冷凍庫深處，不要放門邊。
用冷水沖調並冰過再喝，冰的比較好喝。
一次只調一週內喝得完的量。
如果只是要拿來料理或調酒，把調好的果汁凍成冰塊很方便。

faq.q: 冷凍濃縮柳橙汁可以放多久？
faq.a: 原罐密封放 −18 °C 冷凍，自購買日起 12 個月。

faq.q: 調好的濃縮汁可以放多久？
faq.a: 開封、加水調好之後，冷藏 4 °C 以下最多 1 週。

faq.q: 退冰過的濃縮汁可以再冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 不行。請直接沖調好、放冷藏，並在沖調後果汁的期限內喝完。
